mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is computed continuously without a threshold activation condition.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market that reduces recession risk and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust economic activity, reducing recession risk and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in the past month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth rate > 2.5% annualized in the past quarter), equity markets become overvalued due to excessive optimism, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% (annualized) in the past quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDP growth rate > 2.5% (annualized) in the past quarter, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (measured by CPIAUCSL) compresses real interest rates and increases monetary tightening risk, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL index rises above 305, it signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 305, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in the past month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-shock recovery regime (defined by UNRATE decline > 0.3pp and PAYEMS rise > 0.5% in the past 3 months), improving labor conditions drive strong equity market growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.3pp and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE falls > 0.3pp and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
